neg-112.title: Towards Characterizing Knowledge Distillation of PPG Heart Rate Estimation Models
neg-112.snippet: Heart rate estimation from photoplethysmography (PPG) signals generated by wearable devices such as smartwatches and fitness trackers has significant implications for the health and well-being of individuals. Based on these results, we provide suggestions for selecting a method according to whether a model is available, the budget for training, and whether stable training is required.

neg-117.title: End-to-End Vision-Language-Action Policies for Autonomous Lunar Rover Docking
neg-117.snippet: Surface navigation on the Moon is subject to extreme illumination contrast and deployment-time perceptual disturbances. While modular navigation pipelines have long supported planetary rover navigation, robustness is compromised by measurement errors that propagate through hand-engineered components. End-to-end learned policies are an alternative approach to navigation, which maps observations directly to control actions without intermediate components. Vision-language-action models, in particular, have driven significant breakthroughs in robotics and autonomous vehicle research. By leveraging internet-scale vision-language pretraining, these models can be exploited for their commonsense reasoning and visual understanding to provide robust generalization with limited task-specific data. However, their applicability and performance have yet to be characterized for lunar surface operations. In this study, we design a vision-language-action policy for autonomous lunar rover docking and characterize its performance relative to a modular navigation pipeline. neg-118.snippet: Traffic sign detection plays a vital role in intelligent transportation systems, supporting the safe operation of advanced driver assistance systems and autonomous vehicles. Despite significant progress in real-time object detection, accurately identifying traffic signs under challenging conditions remains difficult. Variations in lighting, adverse weather, motion blur, and partial occlusion often reduce detection performance, especially for small or visually degraded signs where important spatial information can be lost. To address these challenges, we propose Squeeze-Aware-YOLO, a lightweight traffic sign detection framework that introduces a multi-branch bottleneck module combining convolutional kernels of different sizes with a Squeeze-and-Excitation mechanism to improve feature extraction and adaptive channel weighting. In addition, we integrate the Multi-Branch Auxiliary Feature Pyramid Network and Re-parameterized Heterogeneous Multi-Scale modules to strengthen multi-scale feature representation and feature fusion while preserving real-time inference efficiency for practical deployment. neg-118.title: Tracking the Invisible: Self-Supervised Wheel Track Detection with Thermal-RGB Fusion
neg-118.snippet: Accurate detection of drivable area is essential for autonomous driving and advanced driver assistance systems. While state-of-the-art methods focus on general traversability estimation, they prove inadequate for snow-covered roads where following existing wheel tracks offers crucial advantages: improved traction, predictable vehicle dynamics, and verified path stability. To address this, we propose a low-cost, self-supervised approach detecting safety-critical wheel tracks using synchronized RGB-I (RGB + Long-Wave Infrared) imagery. Our method automatically generates training labels by projecting future wheel trajectories from recorded GNSS data. A neural network is designed to identify wheel tracks with the 4-channel RGB-I images from challenging, white-out road surfaces. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in visually monotonous and featureless adverse environment, offering a robust and cost-effective alternative for winter autonomy. The newly introduced ThermalTrack dataset is available at: https://digitalcommons.mtu.edu/thermaltrack/.

Crowdsourced approaches based on fleets provide a promising alternative for continuously validating and updating map information. However, the relationship between the number of contributing vehicles and the quality of the resulting map remains poorly understood. neg-118.title: Traffic Sign Recognition for Autonomous Driving Using Branched YOLOv2 and Geometric Features
neg-118.snippet: Traffic sign recognition (TSR) is an important perception task for autonomous driving and advanced driver-assistance systems, where a system must both localize traffic signs and determine their semantic classes efficiently. This work presents a TSR system based on YOLOv2 for simultaneous detection and classification. Two complementary modifications are studied. First, YOLOv2 is extended with intermediate prediction layers, forming a branched architecture that can terminate inference early for easy cases and reduce computation time. An unsupervised Bayesian image-segmentation method produces binary representations that are compared with class-specific geometric templates inside YOLOv2 bounding boxes. This information is used either during inference or as an additional signal during training. A dedicated dataset is constructed by combining GTSDB and GTSRB samples using seamless cloning and controlled image transformations. neg-118.snippet: Image registration is a vital preprocessing step in multimodal perception tasks, including image fusion, object detection, and semantic segmentation. In Advanced Driver- Assistance Systems (ADAS), spatial misalignment between visible (RGB) and infrared (IR) cameras -caused by non-coincident optical axes and field-of-view differences- introduces non-uniform parallax and visual ghosting. Classical keypoint-based methods are restricted to global homographies that fail under dynamic depth, while unconstrained dense flow algorithms lack structural regularization and suffer from temporal instability. In this paper, we propose XCalib, an unsupervised dense thermal-visible registration framework that bridges this gap. Rather than serving as an absolute metric calibration tool, XCalib leverages virtual pinhole camera parameterization strictly as a geometric constraint space. By optimizing effective relative pose and intrinsics alongside predicted monocular metric depth, XCalib restricts the search space of spatial displacements to physically valid projection geometries. neg-119.snippet: Significant efforts are currently being directed toward the implementation of large-scale quantum information processors, but realizing useful quantum advantage also requires the development of efficient quantum algorithms. While for many practical problems the dominant resource costs are associated with a small set of computational primitives, optimizing them in the quantum setting presents unique challenges, including a reversibility constraint absent from ordinary classical computation. Here we introduce an evolutionary framework in which large language models (LLMs) propose circuit designs and an independent evaluator verifies and scores them. We apply this framework to tasks spanning numerical computation, chemistry, optimization, quantum simulation, and number theory. In seven of the eight tasks, the discovered circuits significantly reduce both Toffoli and qubit counts relative to the state of the art. neg-119.title: SynDebug: A Framework to Debug Logic Bugs in Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing Programs
neg-119.snippet: Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) introduces substantial systems-level complexity through quantum error correction (QEC), making debugging FTQC programs challenging. Existing quantum debugging approaches primarily target logical-level circuits and do not naturally support debugging within realistic FTQC execution flows. We present SynDebug, the first systems-level debugging framework for FTQC programs. SynDebug introduces lightweight assertion-based debugging primitives that operate directly within encoded FTQC infrastructures while avoiding additional logical surface area and minimizing temporal overhead. We evaluate SynDebug across multiple QEC code families, code distances, and encoded workloads, including state preparation, entanglement validation, and Shor-style programs. Our results demonstrate that SynDebug enables practical FTQC debugging with an average 1.8% additional circuit depth overhead (0% in most cases) and no measurable increase in the logical error rate, showing that systems-level debugging for large-scale FTQC applications is both feasible and practical.

neg-119.title: Programmable all-to-all entangling gates for cavity-coupled atoms
neg-119.snippet: Fault tolerant quantum computers greatly benefit from having both high fidelity entangling gates and a non-local qubit connectivity. However, most entangling gates for neutral atoms are local, requiring separated atoms to be moved using optical tweezers to yield entanglement between them. Here, we design a high fidelity Mølmer Sørensen-like entangling gate between neutral atoms coupled to a photonic cavity, enabling a programmable all-to-all connectivity through the shared cavity coupling. The gate is both robust to changes in cavity photon number, and enables selective entanglement between any subset of separated atoms through local laser addressing. This eliminates the need to physically move atoms to perform the gate, and therefore motional errors and erasure are suppressed. Using experimentally realistic parameters we demonstrate gate fidelities exceeding $F > 0.99$, with higher fidelities achievable through optimal control of the pump amplitudes.

neg-119.title: Energetics of Fault-Tolerant Spin-Qubit Quantum Computation
neg-119.snippet: Semiconductor spin qubits offer a promising route to compact and scalable quantum computers, combining long coherence times in isotopically purified silicon with compatibility with semiconductor manufacturing. We evaluate the power and energy requirements of a Loss-DiVincenzo spin-qubit quantum computer by analyzing the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) and benchmarking it against the classical Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). We develop a detailed energy budget, identifying cryogenic cooling as the dominant baseline contribution before quantum error correction (QEC). The comparison between the QFT and the classical FFT reveals that, for any quantum workload operating under a polynomially bounded sampling regime, the crossover in energy consumption occurs at smaller problem sizes than the crossover in execution time. Thus, quantum computing can become energetically competitive before achieving a speedup in execution time. Yet, the variability of sources such as solar photovoltaics requires additional operational flexibility to deliver these services. In this context, hybrid energy storage systems (HESSs) offer an appropriate solution, because different technologies with complementary characteristics can be applied and leveraged to share the power demand and improve the overall performance. neg-120.snippet: Electrification of urban bus systems is expected to accelerate due to its clear environmental benefits. However, effective electric bus deployment requires planning tools that can support decision-making on electrification strategies while balancing operational feasibility, costs, environmental benefits, and impacts on the local electricity grid. Such planning depends on the availability of detailed transit data, which remain scarce in many cities, particularly in developing countries. To address this gap, we present GTFS4EV, an open-source framework that uses publicly available General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) data to simulate bus operations and evaluate electrification scenarios. The framework provides quantitative insights across multiple dimensions. It estimates the minimum onboard battery capacity required for each bus, alongside charging infrastructure needs, economic and environmental impacts, and the potential for solar photovoltaic integration. neg-120.snippet: The increasing integration of distributed energy resources introduces new challenges for accurate fault detection and classification in distribution networks. This paper presents a topology-aware graph convolutional network-based model for fault classification under inverter-induced harmonic distortion. The model uses pre-fault and post-fault voltage and current phasors, including harmonic components, mapped to the IEEE 34-bus system topology. A differential evolution algorithm is employed to optimize the hyperparameters of the network, resulting in a three-layer model that achieves an F1-score of 0.98. neg-120.title: Transfer Learning with Conformalized Quantile Regression for Solar PV Forecasting Under Load-Shedding-Driven Data Scarcity
neg-120.snippet: Solar photovoltaic (PV) forecasting in regions affected by load shedding is challenging because reliable historical observations are scarce. This study proposes a transfer learning framework combined with Conformalized Quantile Regression (CQR) to improve PV power forecasting and provide reliable uncertainty estimates under severe data scarcity. A source-domain PV dataset from Alice Springs, Australia, is used to pretrain a temporal forecasting model, which is then adapted to simulated Bangladesh PV data representing different levels of historical availability. Experimental results show that transfer learning reduces RMSE by up to 23.7% when only one month of target-domain data is available and by 13.7% with three months of data. The proposed Transfer Learning plus CQR framework achieves 94.3% empirical coverage with three months of target data while producing prediction intervals that are 14% narrower than those obtained without transfer learning. These results demonstrate that combining transfer learning with conformal uncertainty quantification can improve both point forecasting accuracy and uncertainty reliability when target-domain PV data are severely limited.

neg-120.snippet: Designing effective and fiscally sustainable policies for solar photovoltaic (PV) adoption requires balancing adoption gains against public expenditure under uncertainty and heterogeneous decision-making. This study formulates PV policy design as a sequential decision problem and integrates reinforcement learning (RL) with a stochastic agent-based model (ABM) that simulates yearly solar PV adoption under uncertainty. A policymaker agent selects annual incentives, including capital grants, subsidised loan rates, and feed-in tariffs, over a 16-year horizon. Adoption--cost trade-offs are explored by varying policy preferences within a scalarised reward framework. Policies are learned using PPO, SAC, and TD3 and evaluated under stochastic simulation. The results show that this approach produces a clear trade-off structure: the highest-adoption policy (TD3, $w_{\text{cost}}=0.5$) achieves approximately 4,145 adopters at a cost of EUR 41.73 million, while the lowest-cost policy (PPO, $w_{\text{cost}}=2.0$) reduces expenditure to EUR 7.27 million with 2,682 adopters. neg-120.title: LLM-Assisted Behavioural and Scenario Augmentation for Agent-Based Energy Adoption Models

This work presents a modular internet of things (IoT) device based on the ESP32 microcontroller integrating temperature, humidity, luminosity, and solar irradiance sensors in an IP68-rated enclosure at a total hardware costs of about \$65~USD when components are sourced in Germany. neg-120.title: Quantification and Surrogate Model Estimation of Spatial-Temporal Carbon Intensity Factors
neg-120.snippet: The transition toward sustainable urban infrastructure is driving a rapid increase in distributed energy resources, particularly among prosumers equipped with solar photovoltaic (PV) installations. Such PV systems are highly dependent on solar radiation, which fluctuates over time and across different city districts, leading to substantial spatial and temporal variations in local carbon intensity factors. The carbon intensity factor is a critical parameter for optimizing energy consumption and reducing emissions in context of smart building control, electric vehicle charging or district heating systems. Hence, high-resolution information on local carbon intensity factors is crucial for intelligent control strategies that minimize environmental impact across urban infrastructures. In this paper, we introduce a novel approach for calculating spatially and temporally resolved carbon intensity factors on an urban district level. neg-120.title: Productive Curtailment in Agrivoltaic Systems under Flexible Interconnection Agreements
neg-120.snippet: Flexible interconnection agreements are increasingly used to streamline the distributed generation interconnection process by limiting real power exports and avoiding costly grid upgrades. Agrivoltaic systems--solar photovoltaic (PV) panels installed over agricultural land--can provide added value under these agreements by adjusting the PV panels away from sun tracking while increasing the sunlight available to crops. This technical note investigates the operation of agrivoltaics under flexible interconnection limits and evaluates their impact on both PV energy production and crop outcomes. We formulate an optimization problem that determines the time-varying tilt of a single-axis tracking agrivoltaic system to maximize energy production subject to a real power export limit over an entire growing season. The resulting PV operating schedules are then used to evaluate PV energy production and crop yield. In a case study, we demonstrate that agrivoltaic systems can comply with flexible interconnection agreements through operational adjustments that improve crop yield, distinguishing them from conventional PV systems that rely solely on inverter curtailment.

neg-121.title: Intelligent Degradation Monitoring in Lithium-ion Batteries via Discharge Incremental Capacity Feature Estimation
neg-121.snippet: Accurate and timely detection of degradation in lithium-ion batteries is crucial to ensure safety, reliability, and longevity in high-demand applications such as electric vehicles and energy storage systems. This paper proposes a novel neural network-based framework that predicts discharge IC features directly from charging signals, eliminating the need for low-current discharge. Trained on a comprehensive dataset of 53 battery cells cycled under diverse fast-charging protocols, the model demonstrates robust generalization ability, effectively estimating degradation indicators on unseen battery data. neg-121.title: Recursive Parameter Identification of Nonlinear Stochastic State-Space Models via Sequentialized Ensemble Kalman Inversion
neg-121.snippet: Recursive parameter identification in nonlinear stochastic state-space models is challenging because unknown parameters affect the measurements through latent-state dynamics. This paper develops a sequentialized ensemble Kalman inversion method for recursive parameter identification from streaming measurements. The proposed method represents the parameter posterior by an evolving ensemble and updates it sequentially as new measurements become available. For each parameter ensemble member, implicit particle filtering is used to approximate the predictive observation statistics required for parameter correction. This formulation enables recursive parameter learning. The method is evaluated on a strongly nonlinear benchmark, with comparison to several existing methods, and then on a nonlinear double-capacitor lithium-ion battery model. The numerical results demonstrate accurate recursive parameter identification and latent-state estimation.

neg-122.snippet: Longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) can reveal disease-progression structure, while useful forecasting requires leakage-controlled discovery, censor-aware outcomes, and inspectable trajectory evidence. neg-122.snippet: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without data centralization but struggles with incentive alignment, accountability, and robustness under heterogeneous non-IID data. Existing decentralized FL (DeFL) systems leverage blockchains for coordination yet face high on-chain overhead, unverifiable self-reports, and weak fairness guarantees. We present the FLAI Protocol, a trusted execution environment (TEE)-backed DeFL framework that integrates enclave-validated aggregation, sparse Peer Evaluation Graph (sPEG) scoring, and on-chain settlement. sPEG incorporates peer-based quality, class coverage, promptness, effort, and reputation into composite contribution scores. The protocol formalizes contribution evaluation and tokenized incentive distribution, ensuring verifiable fairness and resilience against free-riding and collusion. We evaluate FLAI on image, text, and healthcare datasets and demonstrate parity with FedAvg in utility while improving fairness and accountability. neg-122.title: Sequence Composition in EHR Foundation Model Pretraining
neg-122.snippet: Autoregressive electronic health record (EHR) foundation models predict the next event token in patient trajectories: sequences of structured medical events. A typical pretraining strategy is to concatenate all trajectories into a global stream and sample token windows from it. This gives patients with longer sequences more training exposure and allows tokens to attend across patient boundaries. We argue that these choices create a misalignment between pretraining and downstream clinical tasks. To explore this, we investigate how the composition of pretraining sequences affects clinical prediction performance. Using the global-stream approach as a baseline, we propose alternative sequence composition methods that control how patient trajectories contribute to pretraining sequences. Across four MIMIC-IV v2.2 tasks, our best method improves macro AUROC, AUPRC, F1, and balanced accuracy, with relative gains of 9.3% in F1 and 2.7% in AUPRC under a fixed training recipe. neg-122.snippet: Real-world studies (RWS) analyze routinely collected healthcare data, such as electronic health records and insurance claims, to estimate treatment effects, monitor safety, and identify risk factors outside randomized trials. Automating RWS with large language model agents is appealing but brittle: valid analyses depend on dataset-specific clinical semantics, including index dates, follow-up windows, patient/event-level units, and outcome boundaries that are often implicit in observational data. This leads to schema mismatches, temporal errors, inconsistent analytical granularity, and unsupported clinical claims. We present ProCARE, a profile-grounded framework that reformulates RWS automation as constrained compilation. ProCARE converts heterogeneous data profiles into Evidence Contracts specifying available variables, temporal attributes, distributions, and evidentiary limits, and compiles study objectives into RWS-IR, a strongly typed intermediate representation for variables, time relations, analysis units, and statistical tasks. neg-124.snippet: Language embeddings are increasingly used in recommenders to represent item content, but their privacy risks remain poorly understood. neg-124.snippet: Recommender systems often need to balance multiple conflicting objectives. Controllable Multi-Objective Recommendation (CMOR) enables dynamic adjustment of objective trade-offs at inference time without retraining, adapting to shifting user or system requirements. Existing CMOR approaches typically rely on output-level reranking or parameter-generating modules, which either limit the scope of feasible trade-offs or incur substantial training and inference cost. neg-110.snippet: IP anycast lets a service advertise one address from many physical sites, leaving BGP to map each client to a site. It is central to the DNS root server system, public resolvers, and some content delivery networks, yet the same routing mechanism has very different consequences across applications. This paper compares anycast latency in two settings: root DNS, where recursive caching amortizes root-server delay over many users and long time-to-live values, and CDNs, where each additional round trip can directly affect page-load, video-start, or API latency. The synthesis finds that root DNS anycast can exhibit substantial path inflation while still producing limited user-visible delay, whereas CDN anycast requires active engineering of peering, route policy, catchment scope, and measurement feedback to keep inflation small. The paper contributes a comparative latency model, a reproducible measurement design, and an optimization framework that separates resilience-driven anycast objectives from latency-driven objectives. neg-110.title: Exact Mixed-Integer Conic Liftings for Queueing-Based CDN Design
neg-110.snippet: We study a class of content delivery network design problems in which service performance is explicitly modeled through queueing-based response times. In contrast to standard formulations relying on distance-based approximations, the resulting models incorporate congestion effects and give rise to nonlinear expressions involving ratios of affine mappings, reciprocal terms, and interactions across multiple traffic classes. To address these challenges, we develop a systematic framework based on mixed-integer conic liftings that enables exact reformulations of such expressions within a tractable optimization paradigm. The proposed approach combines McCormick-type envelopes and second-order cone representations to derive mixed-integer conic programming formulations that jointly capture geometric design decisions and stochastic service dynamics within the same system. The framework is first introduced in a single-server setting, where the optimal solution exhibits a connection with the classical Fermat--Weber problem, and is then extended to the multi-server case, leading to a general formulation that simultaneously optimizes server locations, capacity allocation, and routing decisions.

neg-110.title: SILC: Lookahead Caching for Short-form Video Delivery Systems
neg-110.snippet: Short video platforms like TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts have gained immense popularity in the last few years and are responsible for a large and growing fraction of Internet traffic. We identify two unique opportunities for improving short video delivery using their existing interactions with content delivery networks (CDNs). First, short videos use a push-based recommendation system, where the user is presented a sequence of videos recommended by the algorithm rather than user explicitly picking content to watch (e.g., in YouTube). Such push-based short video systems offer a unique opportunity for system design by providing visibility into upcoming requests. Second, the popularity of these videos follows a highly skewed Pareto distribution, leading to geographical and temporal overlap amongst videos being served. We leverage these opportunities to build SILC - a lookahead-aware caching system, aimed at (i) reducing CDN cache miss rates, as well as (ii) reducing midgress bandwidth between the CDN and the origin server. Our evaluation of SILC uses traces that we collect from real users, through (i) an in-person user study, and (ii) a data donation program involving 10

neg-110.title: A systematic review of secure coded caching
neg-110.snippet: In a content delivery network (CDN), resources are strained during peak-time and underutilised in off-peak times when supplying digital content to users. Caching can help balance this. At the off-peak time some content is delivered to users' local caches. During peak time, the use of cached data to serve users' requests relieves strain on the network by reducing repeated transfer of popular content. In \emph{coded caching}, the cache content placement is designed in conjunction with the delivery techniques to optimise network throughput. Since dissemination of information, as well as the delivery of entertainment, is reliant on CDNs, the security and privacy of cache placement, user demand, and content delivery, are paramount. In much of the literature in \emph{secure coded caching}, security is built on top of solutions that have efficiency in mind, and most current proposals focus on the security of individual parts of the process. A lack of a unifying network model also makes it difficult to compare or combine solutions. neg-126.title: Enterprise Process Control Tower for IT-Led Improvement
neg-126.snippet: Enterprise integration traffic in large Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems move through Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) and the Intermediate Document (IDoc), and the operational tools that surround that traffic remain fragmented. neg-126.title: ERPBench: A State-Grounded Evaluation Paradigm for Computer-Use Agents in Enterprise Software
neg-126.snippet: Computer-use agents that operate through screenshots and simulated actions are advancing rapidly, yet their evaluation remains anchored to general desktop and web tasks. We introduce ERPBench, a benchmark that evaluates screenshot-only agents on a live and reproducible system and scores each task against ground-truth values in its database. neg-126.snippet: Pharmaceutical sales forecasts inform planning across products, regions, and distribution channels, yet their interpretation depends on inventory availability, transaction semantics, product lifecycle, and the information available when each forecast is issued. neg-126.snippet: Agentic engineering systems have shown strong performance on general-purpose benchmarks, yet their effectiveness in enterprise resource planning (ERP) domain-specific languages (DSLs) remains underexplored. neg-126.title: Agentic ERP: Multi-Agent Large Language Model Architecture for Autonomous Enterprise Resource Planning
neg-126.snippet: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems record transactions reliably but still delegate almost all operational decision-making to human specialists, because classical rule-based automation cannot reason about exceptions and monolithic AI assistants degrade when asked to coordinate across functional boundaries. neg-126.title: ERP Data Provisioning Financial Control Testing
neg-126.snippet: Financial control testing increasingly depends on representative enterprise resource planning (ERP) data in quality environments, yet direct production copies expose personal, supplier, banking, and commercially sensitive records. neg-128.title: Editorial: Navigating the convergence of AI and the Metaverse
neg-128.snippet: As we present Volume 5, Issue 2 of <em>Metaverse</em>, we find ourselves at a pivotal juncture where artificial intelligence (AI) and the metaverse intersect, heralding transformative changes across various domains. The convergence of AI and the metaverse is not merely a technological phenomenon but a philosophical and cultural shift that reflects humanity’s aspirations for a more interconnected and intelligent future. As Alan Turing, often regarded as the father of AI, stated, “Instead of trying to produce a program to simulate the adult mind, why not rather try to produce one which simulates the child’s?” [1]. This underscores the boundless possibilities of creativity and learning inherent in AI—qualities that now extend into the immersive landscapes of the metaverse.

neg-129.snippet: This paper argues that the challenge managers face today when trying to justify investments in sustainability is reminiscent of the challenge of investing in quality management in the 1980s. neg-129.snippet: The purpose of this paper is to address a fundamental flaw in prominent approaches to managing businesses for sustainability. neg-131.title: Settling the Approximability of Submodular Facility Location
neg-131.snippet: In submodular facility location (SFL), introduced by Svitkina and Tardos (SODA 2006), clients $\cal C$ in a metric space are assigned to facilities $\cal F$. A facility serving a set $S \subseteq \cal C$ of clients incurs cost $g(S)$, where $g$ is a monotone submodular function common to all facilities. The best known approximation factor for SFL is $O(\log\log|\cal C|)$, due to Abbasi, Adamczyk, Bosch-Calvo, Byrka, Grandoni, Sornat, and Tinguely (ICALP 2024), improving on the $O(\log|\cal C|)$-approximation of Svitkina and Tardos. We show that this is best possible up to a constant factor in the value-oracle model by showing that there exists no algorithm with only polynomially many queries to $g$ with approximation ratio $o(\log\log|\cal C|)$. This bound holds for algorithms with unlimited computation time, and when $g$ is restricted to matroid rank functions. We also show that the natural linear programming relaxation has an integrality gap of $Θ(\log\log|\cal C|)$. Our lower bound follows by constructing an extension of Vondrák's symmetry-gap approach (FOCS 2009) for matroid rank functions.

neg-132.title: Does Machine Translation Retain Media Bias?
neg-132.snippet: Within the most recent two decades, machine translation (MT) has been advanced from a research area to a mature, deployed technology for prose text and most language pairs. However, language has different dimensions of meaning, and the alluded progress has primarily been demonstrated for propositional meaning. In this small exploratory study, we investigate whether one type of affective meaning, namely different types of linguistically expressed media bias, are retained under automatic translation for two language pairs, English and German as the source languages, and Bulgarian as the target language. Our empirical findings are consistent with the claim that MT does not fully retain existing news bias of its input source text, but also may add extra bias of its own. neg-133.title: SEA-HELM Audio: Evaluating Multilingual ASR-LLM Pipeline Performance Across SEA-HELM Subsets
neg-133.snippet: We introduce SEA-HELM Audio, a Southeast Asian (SEA) multilingual evaluation framework that extends the text-based SEA-HELM benchmark to assess performance degradation in cascaded automatic speech recognition and large language model (ASR-LLM) pipelines. Using synthesized speech, we compare speech-input and text-input performance across five languages (Chinese, English, Malay, Indonesian, and Tamil) on multiple-choice reasoning and instruction-following tasks. We evaluate open-weight and commercial ASR-LLM systems using identical verifiers and quantify the speech gap as the difference between text and speech accuracy. Results show substantial degradation, with accuracy drops of 9.00 to 18.50 percentage points for multiple-choice reasoning and 20.00 to 42.86 points for instruction following. Tamil exhibits the largest degradation, exceeding 40 percentage points. Our findings highlight the limitations of text-only benchmarks in predicting voice-agent reliability and demonstrate the value of SEA-HELM Audio for evaluating multilingual voice-agent systems.

neg-133.title: Towards Efficient Simultaneous Inverse Text Normalization with Pretrained Text-to-Text Language Model and Read-Tag-Write Policy
neg-133.snippet: Streaming Inverse Text Normalization (ITN) is vital for converting spoken-form outputs from streaming Automatic Speech Recognition into formatted written text. Existing streaming ITN methods rely on hybrid systems combining neural tagging with expert-crafted finite-state transducer rules, limiting scalability across domains and languages. While end-to-end models offer superior scalability by learning directly from data, standard encoder-decoder architectures are inherently non-streaming due to global attention. In this paper, we propose an efficient streaming end-to-end ITN system, adapting a pretrained text-to-text model to leverage its robust linguistic knowledge. To enable streaming, we introduce architectural adaptations, a specialized training strategy, a Read-Tag-Write decoding policy, and inference optimizations. Experiments on Vietnamese datasets show accuracy comparable to non-streaming baselines, outperforming hybrid methods while satisfying real-time latency requirements.

neg-134.title: Heading Hierarchy Reconstruction for Complex and Long Documents with Level-Wise Multimodal Memory
neg-134.snippet: Vision-language models (VLMs) have been widely adopted for document parsing and optical character recognition (OCR), as they can accurately extract page-level elements. However, downstream applications such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) also require coherent document-level structure. Although these models indicate heading levels using different numbers of preceding ``\#'' symbols, page-by-page prediction often lacks document-level consistency. In practice, input-resolution and context-length constraints make it infeasible for a VLM to jointly process all page images in documents containing tens or hundreds of pages. To address this limitation, we propose a VLM-based framework that incrementally reconstructs heading hierarchies with a \emph{level-wise multimodal memory}. The memory retains a compact subset of all previously processed pages, selected by anchors. Our framework supports flexible anchor selection, and in this work we select the most recent node at each level, allowing the VLM to observe the visual, textual, and layout patterns of headings at every level. neg-134.title: Forensic Text Recovery from Document Thumbnails Using Text-Aware U-Net
neg-134.snippet: Forensic analysis of low-resolution Word thumbnails presents a significant challenge because these artifacts may constitute the only remaining visual evidence of deleted documents. Standard Optical Character Recognition (OCR) tools perform poorly on such severely degraded images, creating a critical bottleneck in forensic evidence recovery. Although deep learning architectures, such as U-Net, can improve visual image quality, models optimized solely using pixel-based loss functions tend to favor visual smoothness over the structural fidelity required for accurate text recognition. To address this limitation, we propose a text-aware restoration framework designed for forensic triage. The proposed approach employs a U-Net architecture guided by a hybrid optimization strategy that integrates pixel-level fidelity with machine-readable text constraints. Specifically, an OCR-based Normalized Levenshtein Distance (NLD) metric is used during model selection to prioritize the recovery of an accurate character topology. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly reduces the NLD, enabling reliable recovery of machine-readable text from severely degraded thumbnails

neg-134.title: From Pixels to Structure: Lightweight Vision-Language Models for Document OCR and Structured JSON Extraction

neg-135.title: Context Matters! Social, Spatial, and Semantic Coordination with an Embodied Agent in Immersive Analytics
neg-135.snippet: Embodied AI agents in Augmented Reality (AR) could enable more natural collaboration in immersive analytics by engaging users through spatial, conversational, and visual interaction. However, designing such agents requires careful attention to context. We propose a preliminary conceptual framework for context-aware design of embodied agents structured around three dimensions of spatial, social, and semantic. This framework is further categorised into embeddedness (how agents are situated in the contexts) and awareness (how agents perceive and respond to the contexts). To explore this, we present Cobot, an embodied AI agent designed as a design probe. Cobot supports context-sensitive interaction through features such as gaze cues, spatial sound, and task-aware behaviour. We reflect on its design and identify implications for future contextaware embodied agents.

neg-135.title: A Black-Box Positioning Solution for Effortless Integration in Wearable Navigation
neg-135.snippet: Accurate localization is critical for a wide range of applications, including navigation, augmented reality, safety management, and healthcare. However, achieving accurate positioning remains challenging, especially in GPS-degraded environments. Pedestrian Dead Reckoning (PDR), which estimates position based on inertial sensor data, offers a promising alternative but typically demands substantial effort in algorithm design and system integration. This complexity often leads to prolonged development timelines and elevated costs. To address these challenges, we present the PDR Sensor (PDRS), a plug-and-play, black-box PDR module optimized for seamless integration into wearable and IoT platforms. PDRS integrates a microprocessor and an inertial measurement unit (IMU) within a compact, low-power module. It executes real-time sensor fusion onboard, providing position updates via standard interfaces (I2C, SPI, UART). Experimental evaluations demonstrate its high robustness, achieving a step detection error of just 0.16% over 1250 steps and a traveled distance error of 1.87% under diverse conditions. The system further exhibits low latency (2.5 ms) and modest power consumption (52.35 mA).

neg-135.title: LICOA: Learning Instruction-Conditioned Optical Actions for Mobile Spatial Augmented Reality

We introduce LICOA to realize this capability. A shared interface maps synchronized external and onboard RGB cameras with robot control state to physical optical actions across pretrained action models. Because instruction-conditioned optical action lacks dedicated training data and a common evaluation protocol, we construct a matched simulation embodiment and a corpus with 150 tasks and 7,500 rendered episodes, then evaluate models trained only on this corpus in previously unseen real-world environments. neg-135.title: ShadAR: Real-time Prompting On-demand Visual Augmentation in Augmented Reality
neg-135.snippet: Augmented Reality can reshape our visual perception (e.g., simulating color blindness) yet such effects are typically pre-programmed by experts, making visual augmentation static and inflexible. We introduce ShadAR, an AR system that allows users to describe expected visual augmentations (e.g., "Blur all people") for changing their vision in real time. ShadAR can graphically manipulate AR passthrough in real time via shader injection. When receiving a user's prompt, ShadAR uses LLMs (GPT5.2) to interpret the user's intent, analyzes the user's view with object detection (YOLOv26), generates a pixel shader, and applies it to the targeted region on AR passthrough. To understand usage patterns, we invited 21 HCI researchers to use ShadAR, identifying four application domains (design, health, productivity, and social interaction) and two prompt-framing patterns: procedural prompts specifying what to modify and how ("Highlight the book."), and end-goal prompts conveying desired mental or behavioral states ("Make me laugh."). neg-135.title: "The Rose Garden Is a Cemetery": Spatial Dissonance and Divergent Public Experiences of an Indigenous Augmented Reality Tour
neg-135.snippet: Community-authored augmented reality (AR) can contest dominant heritage narratives by juxtaposing stories with physical surroundings. We examine the Thámien Ohlone AR Tour, developed with members of the Ohlone Native American community at Mission Santa Clara and Santa Clara University. Combining paired pre/post surveys from 57 participants with collaborative thematic analysis, we compare reception among Ohlone community members, university affiliates, and Mission visitors. Spatial dissonance captures felt tensions when AR challenged familiar campus readings or when surroundings conflicted with Ohlone histories the AR affirmed, such as a garden's significance as a burial ground. Cultural frames shaped interpretation; contemporary people and relationships made Ohlone continuance tangible. Participants appreciated the tour and called for permanent physical acknowledgment. We propose staging reflective encounters, clarifying community-authored meanings, and using AR to prototype public acknowledgment and support community-directed advocacy. These findings foreground relationships to land and place, informed by Indigenous scholarship, in designing and evaluating AR.

neg-136.title: Robot remote control using virtual reality headset: studying sense of agency with subjective distance estimates
neg-136.snippet: Abstract Mobile robots have many applications in the modern world. The autonomy of robots is increasing, but critical cases like search and rescue missions must involve the possibility of human intervention for ethical reasons and safety. In both cases, active control was contrasted with passive observation of the robot's movement. neg-136.title: Towards Interaction Regulation from Human Feedback via Free Energy Minimization
neg-136.snippet: A central challenge across control and learning is the design of mechanisms regulating the interactions between humans and autonomous agents. Inspired by the free energy principle from computational neuroscience, we introduce a control-theoretical framework to integrate human preferences online into an agent policy. We turn the framework into an open control architecture and validate our approach using a human-in-the-loop experimental testbed involving a rover navigating via onboard sensing. The human, remotely located and equipped with virtual reality headsets, shares the same sensory information as the rover. Human preferences are provided to the rover via gestures which introduce both cooperative and competitive interactions between the agent goal and the preferences. The experiments show that interactions are regulated, validating the proposed approach.

neg-136.title: VR-IPS: Virtual Reality Tool for Photic Stimulation in Photosensitive Diagnosis
neg-136.snippet: Photosensitivity is a neurological condition in which the brain generates epileptiform activity in response to visual stimuli. The standardized clinical diagnosis procedure, named Intermitent Photic Stimulation (IPS), involves exposing patients to a white flashing light at different frequencies to provoke this reaction. However, clinical neurophysiologists report that this protocol is insufficient, leading to underdiagnosis. VR-IPS is a flexible visual stimulation tool that extends conventional flashing-light stimulation by incorporating configurable color lights, static and oscillatory motion patterns, and photoprovocative videos. The system comprises a stimulation module that can run on Virtual Reality headsets or on standard monitors, together with a control module that allows clinicians to create, select, and configure visual stimulus, while controlling the whole stimulation procedure.

neg-136.title: Enhancing Eye Movement Biometrics for User Authentication via Continuous Gaze Offset Score Fusion
neg-136.snippet: Eye movement biometrics (EMB) use subject-specific gaze dynamics for user authentication and identification. Recent deep learning-based EMB systems achieve strong performance by modeling temporal eye movement behavior. However, these systems typically overlook continuous gaze offset, despite prior evidence that it contains user-discriminative information. This work examines whether continuous gaze offset can improve biometric performance when combined with existing biometric features. We evaluate linear and nonlinear fusion methods on two publicly available datasets, collected via the lab-grade eye tracker and virtual reality headset across multiple tasks and observation durations. Results indicate that fusion offers performance benefits on both datasets, particularly when using nonlinear fusion. Additionally, fusing biometric information across multiple tasks further improves authentication performance. These findings support the hypothesis that continuous gaze offset may serve as useful auxiliary information under conditions of degraded or noisy eye tracking.

neg-136.title: SpatialNet with Binaural Loss Function for Correcting Binaural Signal Matching Outputs under Head Rotations
neg-136.snippet: Binaural reproduction is gaining increasing attention with the rise of devices such as virtual reality headsets, smart glasses, and head-tracked headphones. Achieving accurate binaural signals with these systems is challenging, as they often employ arbitrary microphone arrays with limited spatial resolution. The Binaural Signals Matching with Magnitude Least-Squares (BSM-MagLS) method was developed to address limitations of earlier BSM formulations, improving reproduction at high frequencies and under head rotation. However, its accuracy still degrades as head rotation increases, resulting in spatial and timbral artifacts, particularly when the virtual listener's ear moves farther from the nearest microphones. In this work, we propose the integration of deep learning with BSM-MagLS to mitigate these degradations. A post-processing framework based on the SpatialNet network is employed, leveraging its ability to process spatial information effectively and guided by both signal-level loss and a perceptually motivated binaural loss derived from a theoretical model of human binaural hearing. neg-136.title: The Monado SLAM Dataset for Egocentric Visual-Inertial Tracking
neg-136.snippet: Humanoid robots and mixed reality headsets benefit from the use of head-mounted sensors for tracking. While advancements in visual-inertial odometry (VIO) and simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) have produced new and high-quality state-of-the-art tracking systems, we show that these are still unable to gracefully handle many of the challenging settings presented in the head-mounted use cases. Common scenarios like high-intensity motions, dynamic occlusions, long tracking sessions, low-textured areas, adverse lighting conditions, saturation of sensors, to name a few, continue to be covered poorly by existing datasets in the literature. In this way, systems may inadvertently overlook these essential real-world issues. To address this, we present the Monado SLAM dataset, a set of real sequences taken from multiple virtual reality headsets. We release the dataset under a permissive CC BY 4.0 license, to drive advancements in VIO/SLAM research and development.

neg-136.title: Self-supervised Learning of Latent Space Dynamics
neg-136.snippet: Modeling the dynamic behavior of deformable objects is crucial for creating realistic digital worlds. While conventional simulations produce high-quality motions, their computational costs are often prohibitive. Subspace simulation techniques address this challenge by restricting deformations to a lower-dimensional space, improving performance while maintaining visually compelling results. However, even subspace methods struggle to meet the stringent performance demands of portable devices such as virtual reality headsets and mobile platforms. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a novel subspace simulation framework powered by a neural latent-space integrator. Our approach leverages self-supervised learning to enhance inference stability and generalization. By operating entirely within latent space, our method eliminates the need for full-space computations, resulting in a highly efficient method well-suited for deployment on portable devices. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on challenging examples involving rods, shells, and solids, showcasing its versatility and potential for widespread adoption.

neg-137.snippet: Technological progress can give rise to new loss exposures or reduce existing risks. In either case, it strongly affects insurance companies' existing lines of business. As the magnitude of such effects is often closely connected to the innovation's market penetration, reliably predicting its adoption process is vital in enabling insurers to adapt their business strategy accordingly. To tackle this challenge, we propose a novel combination of contributions from the domain of innovation diffusion. Our methodology generates adoption scenarios that holistically account for different sources of uncertainty, offers a structured way to incorporate expert judgment and insights from pre-existing technologies, and updates its predictions as new information on the technology's diffusion becomes available. Its modular nature ensures that components can be easily replaced by suitable alternatives. Using publicly accessible data on privately-owned battery electric vehicles in Germany, the application of our approach for predicting changes to insurance losses and for supporting insurers' sustainability strategies is visualized in a motor insurance case study.

neg-137.title: Rethinking electrified transportation: The case for dynamic wireless charging
neg-137.snippet: Long-term infrastructure investment often requires choosing between an established technology and a capital-intensive alternative that gains value as demand matures. For electric vehicle (EV) charging, this trade-off is between incumbent stationary charging technology and emerging dynamic wireless charging (DWC). DWC could fundamentally alter transportation electrification by enabling high-throughput charging in motion and reducing reliance on large onboard batteries; however, its high upfront cost makes the timing and location of deployment critical. Overcommitting to stationary charging stations (SCS) risks technological lock-in and forgoing the benefits of DWC, whereas premature DWC deployment can strand capital in underutilized corridors. Through a joint investment assessment framework coupling DWC, SCS, and supporting grid infrastructure across nearly 49,000 miles of the US Interstate freight network, we find that higher utilization and longer project lifetimes rapidly shift investment toward DWC, whose share rises sharply from 48% at a project lifetime of 30 years to 100% at 32 years. neg-137.title: Non-Potential Congestion Games with a Continuum of Players
neg-137.snippet: We study a class of congestion games with a continuum of heterogeneous players and a finite set of resources, without assuming the existence of a potential function. Players differ in their individual characteristics and may contribute differently to congestion, which is represented through general aggregate features of the population choosing each resource. We characterize the conditions under which such a game admits a potential and show that this structure generally fails when players have heterogeneous impacts on congestion. To analyze the non-potential case, we introduce the concept of Stochastic Variational Nash Equilibrium, in which players observe idiosyncratic cost shocks before selecting a resource. We show that equilibrium choices are pure conditional on players' characteristics and shock realizations, whereas the induced aggregate allocation is probabilistic. Under Gumbel-distributed shocks, the equilibrium is equivalent to a continuum-player logit Quantal Response Equilibrium. neg-137.title: Co-Optimization of Scheduling, Control, and Incentivization of Electric Vehicles for Improving Power System Stability
neg-137.snippet: We present a finite-horizon, greedy heuristic-based co-optimization and optimal control framework that jointly determines the optimized charging rates, charging times, and an optimal charging control law for electric vehicles (EVs) to improve both voltage stability and small-signal dynamic performance of a power distribution system. The proposed strategy encourages EV drivers to be flexible in choosing their charging rates and times through monetary incentivization under a fixed budget. The design is validated using the IEEE 33-bus distribution system model with ten EV charging stations (EVCSs). Results show that incentivizing drivers to settle for lower charging rates, implemented by a wait-and-save strategy, and rescheduling their charging times strategically can significantly improve the voltage stability index (VSI) of the system as well as the damping factors for the mid-frequency oscillation modes seen in the DC-link bus voltage.

Recent work has shown disagreement between the expected and actual number of binaries with long orbital periods in omega ω $\omega$ Centari. The cluster likely contains a large population of stellar-mass black holes, but so far none have been detected. In this work, we utilize data from a new astrophotometric catalog of stars in omega ω $\omega$ Centauri to perform an astrometric search for binaries, especially those with potential black hole companions. Using synthetic observations of simulated binaries, we measure the detection efficiency of our approach. neg-138.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
neg-138.snippet: Personalization is essential for general-purpose robots to transition into household environments and achieve true practicality. While general robotic manipulation has been extensively studied, personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM) lacks a controlled benchmark for separating task completion from preference satisfaction. We introduce LIBERO-PeRM, a benchmark for preference learning in embodied agents. LIBERO-PeRM studies five questions: 1) how policies follow preferences in zero-shot settings; 2) how they learn single preferences from demonstrations; 3) how efficiently they acquire preferences as demonstrations increase; 4) how learned preferences generalize across layouts and tasks; and 5) how policies compose preferences and behave under conflicts. We propose a controlled formulation and taxonomy of observable preferences in simulation, covering motion, skill, and user-profile choices. This formulation is restricted to language-expressible preferences that can be instantiated in LIBERO without changing the task goal, evaluated automatically, and reused across tasks. Building on LIBERO, our procedural pipeline generates paired demonstrations with and without preferences. We crea

neg-138.title: Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers
neg-138.snippet: We introduce Gen4P, a unified framework for recovering 4D geometry and motion from monocular video. We show that a pretrained video generator can be repurposed into a feed-forward 4D perceiver without iterative denoising. Building on on-demand querying, Gen4P processes clean video latents in a single encoder pass and predicts the requested 4D attributes through a lightweight cross-attention decoder. The on-demand query formulation enables flexible spatial sampling, and our proposed continuous-time queries further provide temporal flexibility. To strengthen geometric knowledge, we propose a straightforward plug-in solution by incorporating a pretrained video-depth LoRA as a frozen geometry prior, improving overall performance without adding extra trainable parameters. Gen4P achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on tasks of 3D point tracking, video depth and camera pose estimation. Qualitative results on in-the-wild videos illustrate its capability of tracking complex motion while maintaining the delicate structure. neg-138.title: Which Tokens to Merge? Diffusion Dynamics for Efficient Image Generation
neg-138.snippet: Token merging has emerged as an effective training-free strategy for accelerating diffusion models by reducing redundant token computation while minimizing generation degradation. A key challenge is determining which tokens can be safely merged and which should be preserved for subsequent computation. Existing method addresses this by preserving prompt-aligned foreground regions, thereby protecting semantically relevant structures. However, this text-relevance criterion overlooks background objects, local details that are not explicitly mentioned in the prompt, leading to degraded structural coherence. In this work, we propose Dynamics-aware Token Merging (DaTMe), a training-free framework that grounds token merging in the underlying diffusion dynamics. Our key insight is that token importance should reflect whether a token remains unresolved during denoising and whether it carries structural information. To this end, DaTMe constructs a dynamics- aware importance map from the Tweedie denoised estimate. neg-138.title: Perceive, Predict, and Plan: a Unified World Action Model for Egocentric Dexterous Manipulation
neg-138.snippet: We introduce P$^{3}$-WAM, a unified world action model for egocentric dexterous manipulation that learns 3D perception, action-conditioned prediction, and goal-directed planning through three complementary modes: Perceive, which reconstructs articulated hand motion and camera trajectories from video; Predict, which generates visual futures under prescribed actions; and Plan, which jointly generates action trajectories and their anticipated visual consequences conditioned on an initial image, a language instruction, and an optional visual goal. Our model integrates a compact, structured 3D action representation into a pretrained video diffusion transformer through a mixture-of-transformers architecture with shared base weights, modality-specific adaptation, and bidirectional visual-action attention. Randomized modality visibility lets video and 3D actions serve as either conditioning context or prediction targets across the three modes. Experiments show that unified training improves all three capabilities over single-mode training, including gains in planning quality under a vision-language model evaluation. Through unified training, our model outperforms specialized baselines on 3

neg-139.title: Estadísticas relacionadas con el feminicidio a nivel mundial
neg-139.snippet: El femicidio, también conocido como feminicidio, es la forma más extrema de violencia de género y se define como el asesinato intencionado de mujeres por el hecho de ser mujeres. El objetivo de la presente investigación consistió en evaluar y comparar las estadísticas de feminicidio a nivel mundial en los últimos ocho años. Se empleó Análisis de varianza y el coeficiente de correlación de Spearman. Al comparar las diferentes tasas de feminicidio en el tiempo (2015-2022), se detectó diferencia altamente significativa entre regiones, donde África ocupa la primera posición seguida de América y Oceanía.

neg-139.title: Formación del Profesor Universitario
neg-139.snippet: Este estudio de revisión tuvo por objetivo caracterizar las principales tendencias relacionadas con la formación del profesor universitario. Se llevó a cabo la búsqueda de la información en el periodo comprendido entre 2000 y 2023 en diferentes fuentes. Se consideraron indicadores relacionados con productividad diacrónica, dominancia temática y concurrencia de palabras clave a fin de ubicar un panorama amplio alrededor del tema. Los resultados evidencian un notable crecimiento de estudios en los últimos años, además, logra reconocerse un vacío respecto a investigaciones orientadas a identidad y subjetividad del profesor universitario, lo cual exhorta la necesidad de ahondar en dicha problemática. Así como, se reconocen avances significativos y grandes desafíos para la formación del profesor de educación superior.

neg-139.title: Latin American Critical Social Sciences and Situated Thinking
neg-139.snippet: The article highlights the dangers of conducting research without being aware of the place of enunciation. It reviews the deformation of the American reality by European science in the 17th and 18th centuries. Subsequently, it illustrates with examples the attempts to overcome this problem in the American eighteenth century, a period that gave rise to a marked interest in investigating the American reality, an endeavor that reached its climax with the emergence of the so-called Social Sciences in the mid-twentieth century. Finally, we reflect on some of the implications of situated and localized thinking. René Zavaleta’s concept of variegation is used for this purpose. It is found that thinking and researching situationally, by attending to specific contexts, avoids losing sight of the heterogeneity and complexity of situated realities. It is something that can also contribute to create emancipatory possibilities.

neg-139.title: Aliarse para gobernar: elecciones locales y regionales en Colombia
neg-139.snippet: Desde la irrupción de la Constitución de 1991 de Colombia, muchos elementos de la dinámica electoral han venido cambiando en este país. Uno de ellos, quizás el más importante, es la trascendencia que han tomado las alianzas electorales para las elecciones locales y regionales. Con un análisis de las elecciones del 2015 y 2019, este artículo describe la forma cómo se conforman las alianzas interpartidistas en estos dos casos. Para esto se acude a un análisis de redes, donde se establecen qué alianzas se han dado, la cantidad de las mismas, los actores que intervienen, entre otros elementos.

neg-139.title: VGM-VS: Rethinking Visual Geometry Model for High-Precision Visual Servoing
neg-139.snippet: We present VGM-VS, a visual servoing method built on a pretrained feed-forward visual geometry model. Given the current view and a reference image captured at the target configuration, we estimate the relative camera pose with a visual geometry model and apply it iteratively as the pose increment of a closed-loop pose-based visual servoing (PBVS) scheme. The geometry-aware representation acquired from large-scale pretraining keeps this estimate reliable when the target is occluded, weakly textured, or covers only a small part of the image. However, the scale ambiguity inherent to these models leaves the predicted translation defined up to an unknown scale, while the pose increment must be metric for robot control. We close this gap with a scene-specific metric adaptation: the robot autonomously records image--pose pairs along a predefined motion starting from the target pose, and we fine-tune the camera head on these data, jointly learning the hand--eye transform and thus removing the need for a dedicated calibration process. We evaluate our method on three real-world assembly tasks with demanding tolerances: USB-C cable picking, cable insertion, and RAM insertion. Running in real

neg-139.title: EgoKit: Towards Unified Low-Cost Egocentric Data Collection with Heterogeneous Devices
neg-139.snippet: Egocentric video is increasingly used as a data source for robot learning, activity understanding, and embodied AI research, but collecting it at scale remains fragmented in practice: each candidate host device, such as an Android phone, iPhone, iPad, smart glasses, or extended reality (XR) headset, exposes a different SDK, a different policy on raw camera access, and different limitations on external USB cameras and on-device tracking. Synchronized ego-view and wrist-view capture is therefore typically obtained by either committing to a single proprietary platform or building one-off rigs that do not transfer across devices. To address this gap, we present EgoKit, a toolkit that exposes the same egocentric recording workflow across six heterogeneous host devices. Across all supported devices, EgoKit presents the same recording interaction and produces locally stored video with a uniform log format; on XR headsets, it additionally logs head pose and OpenXR-standard 26-joint hand tracking aligned to the video streams. The companion accessories, including two wrist cameras with mounts, a head strap, and a USB-C hub, add wrist-view capture to any supported host without custom hardware

neg-139.title: Measuring the usable energy of a USB power bank with an inline USB meter v1
neg-139.snippet: This protocol measures the energy a USB power bank actually delivers at its output port, at a fixed 5 V / 2 A operating point, using an inline USB meter and a constant-current electronic load. Comparing the measured watt-hours with the label watt-hours gives the conversion efficiency; a healthy lithium-ion bank typically delivers 80-90 % of its cell energy, and repeating the test over time tracks capacity fade.

neg-139.title: Investigating How MacBook Accessories Evolve across Generations, and Their Potential Environmental, Economical Impacts
neg-139.snippet: The technological transition of MacBook charging solutions from MagSafe to USB-C, followed by a return to MagSafe 3, encapsulates the dynamic interplay between technological advancement, environmental considerations, and economic factors. This study delves into the broad implications of these charging technology shifts, particularly focusing on the environmental repercussions associated with electronic waste and the economic impacts felt by both manufacturers and consumers. By investigating the lifecycle of these technologies - from development and market introduction through to their eventual obsolescence - this paper underscores the importance of devising strategies that not only foster technological innovation but also prioritize environmental sustainability and economic feasibility. This comprehensive analysis illuminates the crucial factors influencing the evolution of charging technologies and their wider societal and environmental implications, advocating for a balanced approach that ensures technological progress does not compromise ecological health or economic stability.

neg-139.title: Systematization of Knowledge: Security and Safety in the Model Context Protocol Ecosystem
neg-139.snippet: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) has emerged as the de facto standard for connecting Large Language Models (LLMs) to external data and tools, effectively functioning as the "USB-C for Agentic AI." While this decoupling of context and execution solves critical interoperability challenges, it introduces a profound new threat landscape where the boundary between epistemic errors (hallucinations) and security breaches (unauthorized actions) dissolves. This Systematization of Knowledge (SoK) aims to provide a comprehensive taxonomy of risks in the MCP ecosystem, distinguishing between adversarial security threats (e.g., indirect prompt injection, tool poisoning) and epistemic safety hazards (e.g., alignment failures in distributed tool delegation). We analyze the structural vulnerabilities of MCP primitives, specifically Resources, Prompts, and Tools, and demonstrate how "context" can be weaponized to trigger unauthorized operations in multi-agent environments. Furthermore, we survey state-of-the-art defenses, ranging from cryptographic provenance (ETDI) to runtime intent verification, and conclude with a roadmap for securing the transition from conversational chatbots to autonomous age

neg-139.title: Modular multi-axis stepper motor driver with remote control for use in microscopy
neg-139.snippet: Mechanical translation of samples along several axes is often required in microscopy, and automated positioning requires motorizing the translation stages. Stepper motors are commonly employed but require specialized driver electronics for reliable operation. Here we describe a low-cost, open-source controller design that drives several stepper motors and implements important safety features, such as monitoring of mechanical limit switches, stall detection, and protective software limits. If rotational encoders in the motors or linear encoders on the stages are available, the controller can monitor the stage position and correct it in a feedback loop. The stages can be controlled with serial commands via USB, or optionally from a remote control box that incorporates a joystick for real-time multi-axis speed control, rotary dials for fine axis positioning, and a display to indicate the stage positions. To ease adoption, we provide driver libraries in Python and C, a driver for the commonly used microscopy control software $μ$Manager, and an example graphical user interface for calibration and testing.

neg-139.title: Spatially anchored Tactile Awareness for Robust Dexterous Manipulation
neg-139.snippet: Dexterous manipulation requires precise geometric reasoning, yet existing visuo-tactile learning methods struggle with sub-millimeter precision tasks that are routine for traditional model-based approaches. Learning Speech Attribute Representations via Multi-Teacher Distillation
neg-141.snippet: Recent post-training approaches have shown that self-supervised speech encoders can be adapted to learn a single utterance-level speech attribute through knowledge distillation. In this work, we investigate whether a single speech encoder can simultaneously preserve multiple complementary utterance-level speech representations. We propose a multi-attribute multi-teacher distillation framework that learns semantic, speaker, language, and emotion representations from four frozen teacher models using a shared SSL backbone and attribute-specific branches. Experiments on multilingual semantic retrieval, speaker verification, language identification, and speech emotion recognition show that the proposed model achieves performance close to dedicated single-task students while requiring only a single shared encoder. Furthermore, the learned layer aggregation strategies reveal that different speech attributes naturally emerge at different depths of the SSL encoder, providing new insights into the organization of speech representations.

neg-141.title: Aligning LLMs with Sparse Retrieval via Adaptive Sparse Supervision
neg-141.snippet: While large language models (LLMs) offer strong semantic representations, their application to first-stage retrieval incurs substantial latency and storage costs. Neural sparse retrievers such as SPLADE provide efficient retrieval but rely on relatively compact encoders with limited representational capacity. To bridge this gap, we propose an LLM-based sparse retrieval framework with input-adaptive sparse alignment. Specifically, we introduce a dynamic $α$-truncation strategy that selects input-specific supervision supports based on the cumulative activation mass of SPLADE representations. This strategy guides the LLM to preserve salient lexical signals while suppressing less informative activations, without relying on a fixed support budget. Subsequent retrieval fine-tuning combines contrastive learning, knowledge distillation, and sparsity regularization to improve retrieval effectiveness. Experiments on MS MARCO and six selected BEIR datasets demonstrate improvements over SPLADE++ while maintaining competitive effectiveness against LLM-based sparse retrievers. neg-141.title: Clean Data Can Still Carry Backdoors: Support-Persistent Backdoors for Model Reuse
neg-141.snippet: Traditional backdoor attacks inject artificial trigger patterns into training data, causing models to misclassify triggered inputs while maintaining normal behavior on clean samples. Since these artificial triggers are absent in clean datasets, standard knowledge distillation (KD) typically eliminates them, leading to the common belief that KD serves as an effective purification defense. In this paper, we propose DAR (Discover-and-Relabel), a support-persistent backdoor method that retains its behavior even after clean-data distillation. DAR identifies naturally abundant patterns in low-dimensional feature subspaces using subspace clustering and applies label-only poisoning to samples that inherently satisfy the discovered rule. At test time, the backdoor is activated by locally modifying the corresponding subspace of the target images. By instantiating spatial and frequency operators, DAR achieves attack accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art backdoor attacks in ImageNet classification and CLIP-based prompt tuning. Notably, DAR keeps attack success above 96% after clean KD and remains defense-resistant in practice. Project page: https://junhoo.me/backdoor

We measure what each is worth in received power rather than in top-1 accuracy, whose differences of a few points amount to only tenths of a decibel. We use real DeepSense 6G measurements, mainly at one roadside site, and one convolutional-recurrent predictor family evaluated open-loop up to 0.67 s ahead. neg-141.title: PA1-OPD: One-Step Prefix-Augmented On-Policy Distillation for Language Model Pretraining
neg-141.snippet: Knowledge distillation (KD) improves language-model pretraining by matching teacher distributions at corpus prefixes, but provides no direct supervision at contexts induced by student predictions. We introduce PA1-OPD, which augments corpus-path distillation with teacher feedback after one student-sampled transition per selected prefix. This expands the supervised states while retaining next-token prediction and corpus-path KD. Data-anchored roots support parallel sampling, and differentiable tree attention shares prefix computation without changing inference. In two continued-pretraining settings, full coverage improves held-out cross-entropy over KD across C4, PG-19, and Pile at every evaluated checkpoint. In Stage2, selecting the 10% of roots with highest student surprisal adds 48.85% to KD's Macro cross-entropy gain over next-token training. Gains remain when branch supervision excludes successor states already on the corpus path, supporting the value of feedback beyond observed contexts.
